description.text: FactSet Research Systems Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries ("we," "our," "us," the "Company" or "FactSet") was founded in 1978 and has been publicly traded since June 1996. We are dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange ("NYSE") and the NASDAQ Stock Market ("NASDAQ") under the symbol "FDS". FactSet has been a member of the S&P 500 since December 2021.

about.description_short: FactSet (NYSE:FDS | NASDAQ:FDS) supercharges financial intelligence, offering enterprise data and information solutions that help our clients maximize their potential. Our cutting-edge digital platform seamlessly integrates proprietary financial data, client datasets, third-party sources, and flexible technology to deliver tailored solutions across the buy side, sell side, wealth management, private equity, and corporate sectors. With over 48 years of expertise, a presence in 20 countries, and extensive multi-asset class coverage, we leverage advanced data connectivity alongside AI and next-generation tools to streamline workflows, drive productivity, and enable smarter, faster decision-making. Serving more than 9,200 global clients and over 260,000 individual users, FactSet is a member of the S&P 500 dedicated to innovation and long-term client success.

analysis_md:
# FDS — FactSet Research Systems Inc.
Engine 5.5 run, 2026-10-19. In scope (market cap $11.592B at $302.00, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or financials_history.csv — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Global financial data, analytics and workflow subscriptions for investment professionals: workstation and Excel-embedded analytics, data feeds and APIs, portfolio/risk tools, and the CUSIP Global Services securities-identifier business. Revenue is overwhelmingly recurring Annual Subscription Value (ASV). Fiscal year ends August 31. Competitors are Bloomberg, LSEG (Refinitiv) and S&P Capital IQ, plus AI-first entrants such as AlphaSense.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K, period ended 2025-08-31, filed 2025-10-22):** operating cash flow $726,260,000 (ttm.json FY leg); capex $108.8M (key_numbers.md capex basis FY2025: components, PaymentsToAcquireProductiveAssets); SBC $61,229,000 (ttm.json FY leg).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $556.2M = $14.49/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $556.2M, latest FY OE/share $14.49)
- Maintenance version (from financials_history.csv): $520,926,000 — same ballpark as the conservative figure, which raises confidence.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years (key_numbers.md). Net debt (latest) $1.031B; net debt / normalized OE 1.57x (key_numbers.md diagnostics; dcf_numbers.json records 1.88x on the preliminary median base — the 1.57x figure is the final TTM-based run).
- Capex coverage: capex was $60.8M / $85.7M / $108.8M in FY2023/24/25 (key_numbers.md) against D&A of $105,384,000 / $125,187,000 / $157,691,000 in financials_history.csv — capex runs below D&A because the asset base is capitalized software and data infrastructure, not plant; no CAPEX_COVERAGE_LOW flag fired and the cash-flow capex line is fully read (single productive-assets tag in the last two years).

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q3 FY2026 (2026-05-31), from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $726,260,000 − prior YTD $514,160,000 + current YTD $617,492,000 = **TTM $829,592,000**
- Capex: FY $108,806,000 − prior YTD $74,840,000 + current YTD $87,319,000 = **TTM $121,285,000**
- SBC: FY $61,229,000 − prior YTD $47,154,000 + current YTD $61,541,000 = **TTM $75,616,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **36,957,000** — down from 38,385,000 in FY2025 on accelerated buybacks
- **TTM OE total $632,691,000 → base OE/share $17.12** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $14.27/share and the latest FY is $14.49/share; the TTM base is used because the FY is stale (see STALE_FY) and the TTM legs show OCF and buybacks both stepped up after FY2025. No overrides of any kind were declared.

Post-period check (research, not an engine input): FactSet's FY2026 earnings release (reported 2026-09-30; the FY2026 10-K was not yet the engine's latest filing — latest 10-K on file is FY2025, filed 2025-10-22) printed revenue +6.7%, organic ASV +7.0%, free cash flow up ~14.6% and ~$644M of buybacks — consistent with the TTM trend, and FY2027 guidance of revenue +5–6% and organic ASV +5–6.5% anchors the scenario starts below.

## Moat: 6/10 — moderate / narrow, durable but contested
Justification: Embedded workstation/Excel workflows and the CUSIP identifier franchise give real switching costs and >95% ASV retention, with ROIC ~19-20% in FY2023-25 (40%+ before the debt-funded CUSIP acquisition enlarged the capital base) and gross margin stable near 53%; capped at 6 because Bloomberg/LSEG/S&P Global are larger, pricing is the most negotiable of the big four, and generative AI is credibly commoditizing data/workflows outside CUSIP (Morningstar stripped its moat rating to none in March 2026).
- FOR: Switching costs: workstation, Excel model libraries and APIs embedded in client research/portfolio/reporting workflows; migrating model libraries costs clients tens of thousands in analyst time
- FOR: CUSIP Global Services securities-identifier franchise — a near-standard identifier business, the most defensible part of the franchise
- FOR: Retention above 95% of ASV and 47 consecutive years of revenue growth; subscription ASV model is highly recurring
- FOR: ROIC well above cost of capital through the recent cycle (fundamentals.json roic_proxy series: FY2020 43.4%, FY2021 44.6%, FY2022 15.1%, FY2023 18.0%, FY2024 20.2%, FY2025 19.3%) with gross margin stable at ~53-54% (FY2023 53.3%, FY2024 54.1%, FY2025 52.7%, fundamentals.json)
- AGAINST: Bloomberg, LSEG and S&P Global are larger with broader data and network advantages; FactSet pricing is the most negotiable of the four
- AGAINST: Generative AI lowers the cost of replicating data and workflow products outside CUSIP — Morningstar removed FactSet's moat rating in March 2026 on exactly this argument; AI-first entrants such as AlphaSense are attacking the research workflow
- AGAINST: Growth has slowed to mid-single digits (FY2027 guidance: revenue +5-6%, organic ASV +5-6.5%) from a 9.2% 5-year revenue CAGR
- AGAINST: Margin pressure from AI and technology investment: TTM operating margin 29.6% vs 32.2% in FY2025 (fundamentals.json); adjusted operating income rose only ~1.4% in FY2026 despite 7% ASV growth
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 9.8 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check and recalibration (written reason): the engine's blended growth is 6.99% (components: rev CAGR 5y 9.22%, rev CAGR 3y 7.98%, latest rev YoY 5.39%, OE/share CAGR 2y 3.84%; share count CAGR -0.30%, growth adj 0.30%). The default scenario offsets would start the bull case at 12.0% and the super bull at 19.0% — above every recent print and above guidance, with no evidence behind them: latest prints are FY2025 revenue YoY 5.39%, TTM revenue YoY +6.6% (fundamentals.json), Q3 FY2026 organic ASV +7.1%, FY2026 revenue +6.7%, and FY2027 guidance of revenue +5–6% / organic ASV +5–6.5%. Scenario starts were therefore recalibrated via offsets (-0.08 / -0.04 / -0.01 / +0.02 / +0.05 vs g_base) to -1.0 / 3.0 / **6.0** / 9.0 / 12.0% — the base start sits on guidance plus the buyback tailwind already in the TTM share count, the bull start is a return to the 3-5y revenue CAGR range, and even the super bull only assumes a return to roughly the 5-year CAGR plus buybacks. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25 (defaults — the bear multipliers carry the margin-compression risk). Price $302.00.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -1.0% | 0.75 | $90.05 | 6.07% |
| Bear | 25% | 3.0% | 0.90 | $129.12 | 7.87% |
| Base | 30% | 6.0% | 1.00 | $163.96 | 9.44% |
| Bull | 25% | 9.0% | 1.10 | $206.09 | 11.25% |
| Super bull | 10% | 12.0% | 1.25 | $267.56 | 13.71% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $168.75 (-44.1% vs price), IV@12% $225.11, IV@10% $288.10, weighted IRR 9.67%, base-case IRR 9.44%**
- **Tier by numbers: D.** Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 5.67%, terminal value 19.2% of IV@15%, scenario spread 2.97x, net debt 1.57x normalized OE, 13.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing prices (weighted path): 15% at $168.75, 20% at $118.28, 25% at $90.61. Even the super-bull IV@15 ($267.56) sits below the $302.00 price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 14 months ago; 13.6 months since FY end in diagnostics): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q3 FY2026 (2026-05-31, 10-Q filed 2026-07-01), legs quoted above. The FY2026 earnings release (post-period check above) corroborates the TTM direction.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear-case tier D at 7.87% vs bull-case tier C at 11.25%): the verdict is sized to the bear end — the final tier is D, the weighted IRR (9.67%) is itself in the D band, and no scenario at or below the bull case clears even the 15% hurdle at this price.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (preliminary run only, 4.49x): an artifact of the default super-bull growth start (19.0%) that no recent print supports. The recalibrated final run's spread is 2.97x and the flag no longer fires. Confidence is still capped at medium, not high.

## My thoughts / method range
- This is a quality-versus-price result, not a quality dispute: OE positive 5/5 years, retention above 95%, ROIC ~19-20%, buybacks shrinking the diluted count (38,385,000 FY2025 → 36,957,000 current-YTD), and the TTM base ($17.12) is the most generous defensible base — it already credits the post-FY2025 OCF step-up. On the preliminary median base ($14.27) with default offsets the weighted IRR was 8.98% (Tier D); on the TTM base with recalibrated growth it is 9.67% (Tier D). Every defensible method lands in D at $302.
- The honest debate is the moat, not the arithmetic: if generative AI commoditizes the non-CUSIP franchise (Morningstar's March 2026 position), even the bear OE multiplier may prove kind over a 15-year fade; if the switching costs hold and AI products (MCP/API adoption) re-accelerate ASV, the bull path is the ceiling the model allows — and it still does not clear 15% at $302.
- Margin watch: TTM operating margin 29.6% vs 32.2% in FY2025 — the AI/technology spend must convert to ASV or the OE multipliers, not growth, become the binding assumption.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 9.67%; bear D 7.87% → bull C 11.25%)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the filing-derived TTM base and OE quality; medium on the growth path given the AI/moat debate and the not-yet-filed FY2026 10-K)
- One-liner: High-quality subscription compounder, moat 6/10 — does not clear 15% at $302 (weighted IRR 9.7%, weighted IV@15 $168.75); it would clear 15% only below about $169.
